content.value: Cloud GUI Remake — Wave 5 round 9: RUN THE PREDICATE, TAKE THE VERDICT

Living wave Paper for the Cloud GUI Remake epic (bp task task-47bc4168392dec17), round 9 of phase 5. Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md (the epic's law — NOT the rotating bp-cloud-epic-charter.md slot). Predecessor Paper: cloud-gui-remake-wave-2026-07-20-seal-r4.
STATUS: SURVEYING. This Paper is appended by every later phase — Digest adds the survey digest and verify plan, Decide adds the decisions and wave plan, Review closes it as the debrief.
The wish

"RUN THE SEAL PREDICATE AND ABIDE BY IT. The Cloud GUI Remake epic has now attempted to seal SIX times. Round 8 built the thing that ends that: an executable seal predicate, frozen and committed BEFORE any builder flew. This cycle executes it and takes the verdict — SEAL or NO SEAL — without negotiation and without building a seventh instrument."
Hard model constraint: every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet. Decide MUST set builder_model 'opus' for EVERY slice, never 'fable'.
Ground truth, verified at Strategize
The frozen predicate IS on origin/main: cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.mjs, 13,689 bytes. Local and origin copies are byte-identical.

overflow-guard.mjs IS on origin/main, 26,139 bytes. It dispatches on --defect, exits 2 on an unknown defect id (no vacuous pass), and makes real getComputedStyle assertions for all three registered defects.
The GR108/GR109/GR115 fix LANDED as 0261ace15 (#4909). origin/main:cloud/priv/static/app.css:787 carries `.topbar-right > * { min-width: 0; }`.
Live ledger at Strategize: roster 140 children, {open: 77, done: 63}. At round 8's review run it was 139 {in_progress:2, open:74, done:63}. The ledger drifts continuously — GR126.
Round 8's live predicate run returned VERDICT: NO SEAL, real exit 1 — 74 unforwarded rows (clause a) and 3 defects at commit:null (clause b).
All three KNOWN_DEFECTS still carry commit: null. Clause (b) is structurally unsatisfiable until they are registered. gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits owns this and is filed, priority 0.

LOCAL MAIN IS DIVERGED: 4 ahead / 18 behind origin/main, and all 4 are duplicate charter commits whose content is ALREADY on origin. Worse, origin's charter is 239,921 bytes vs local's 234,526 — origin carries the entire round-8 round-1 debrief that local lacks. Any builder basing on local main works from a stale charter.
The inherited dispatch order (from round 8's debrief, origin charter tail)
(1) merge gr-p5r7-tablet-overflow and close its criterion 10 — the MERGE half is DONE (0261ace15); the ledger close is not.
(2) close gr-p5r7-reshoot-verify criterion 8 as 'no PR by design', NOT as abandoned.
(3) gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits — BEFORE any successor work. Skipping it burns the round-2 builder on a structurally impossible green.
(4) then and only then gr-p5r5-successor-seal, running the predicate LAST in its own claim.
Direction: THE SEAL IS A DISCLOSURE, NOT A RENAME

Execute the inherited dispatch order exactly, build NO new instrument, and take the exit code as the verdict. That is the wish, and it is non-negotiable. But the exit code is not the deliverable. The predicate can only measure a mechanical property — 'does this row's parent equal the successor id'. A successor epic with no charter, no triage and no priorities passes clause (a) identically to a great one. What survives this epic is not the exit code; it is whether the next person can READ the ending.
So the wave's product is a seal that means what a reader thinks it means:

ROW-BY-ROW DISPOSITION, NO BULK SWEEP. Each of the ~77 live rows is individually either evidence-closed (with its landed commit named) or forwarded. Rows whose work actually landed — gr-p5r7-tablet-overflow, gr-p5r7-reshoot-verify, gr-p5r8-bpconsole-dead-rule ('FOLDED INTO gr-p5r7-tablet-overflow') — get CLOSED on evidence, not swept into the successor. Bulk-forwarding everything would understate what the epic accomplished and inflate the successor into a junk drawer.

THE SUCCESSOR SHIPS WITH A CHARTER. It inherits triaged into named bands, with the security-shaped rows (gr-blk-oauth-head-mint, gr-blk-sse-token-in-query, gr-backlog-tfa-confirm-throttle, gr-bl-peer-ip-container, gr-backlog-console-redaction-allowlist) named as security-shaped rather than filed as backlog texture.

TRANSIT IS A LEGITIMATE FORWARDING ADDRESS. The frozen predicate reads exactly ONE successor id, so a row routed honestly to a different epic's parent becomes an orphan and fails clause (a). Several live rows are plainly not Cloud GUI at all (worktree-registry bloat, primary-checkout reconciliation, ungoverned Vercel checks, a Studio perf flake). The reconciliation that does not move the bar: re-parent all survivors under the single successor, and the successor's charter records the true onward routing as its first act. 'Forwarding address' is a postal metaphor; transit is what it has always meant.

ONE PERMITTED EDIT TO THE PREDICATE. commit: null becomes a verified SHA — nothing else. Each SHA is verified by DIFF (does 0261ace15 actually contain the fix for THIS defect?), never by commit message, per GR129's precedent. Any other edit to seal-predicate.mjs voids the wave. Round 8 already ruled this is not a freeze violation: the freeze protects the BAR — the clauses, thresholds and guard delegation — while commit is the freeze's own designated input.

THE PREDICATE RUNS LAST, ONCE, ATOMICALLY, by the same agent that finished the ledger — GR126, because two builders writing the ledger concurrently can green a predicate over a half-moved roster. Its verbatim stdout, ISO timestamp and roster count go into the charter as the epic's terminal artifact, whichever way it exits.

NO SEAL IS PRE-AUTHORIZED AND TERMINAL. One repair attempt maximum on a mechanical failure (missing Chrome, absent BP_TOKEN). A substantive failure is the verdict, and the successor is the ending. No seventh instrument, in any disguise.

FIRST ACT, BEFORE ANY BUILDER FLIES: reset local main to origin/main. Four duplicate charter commits sit on local main while origin's charter runs 5,395 bytes ahead. This is the known epic-cycle-commits-charter-to-local-main trap, and it poisons every worktree based on it.
Direction debate

RIVAL 1 — MECHANICAL EXECUTION. Do the four dispatch steps, bulk re-parent the survivors, run, report. The most literal reading of the wish and the cheapest. It wins on 'no seventh instrument' purity. It loses because it produces a seal that is a rename: 74 rows land in an unchartered bucket, several of them mislabeled as Cloud GUI work when they are repo hygiene or Studio, and a reader six months out finds a successor with no story. The predicate cannot detect any of that — which is precisely why the wave, not the instrument, has to supply it.

RIVAL 2 — DISCLOSURE SEAL (WINNER). The same four steps, but every row gets an individual disposition and the successor is chartered and triaged. Costs one slice of judgment work. It wins because the exit code is guaranteed-ish either way — what actually varies between a good and a bad version of this wave is whether the ending is readable.

RIVAL 3 — AUDIT FIRST. Before sealing, spot-audit the 63 done rows for false-done and widen KNOWN_DEFECTS to cover every ledger row that self-describes as user-facing. REJECTED: this is the seventh instrument in disguise. It re-derives the bar after seeing the roster, which is the exact thing the freeze exists to forbid. Its legitimate concern — that clause (b) certifies the word KNOWN over only three hand-registered defects — is already disclosed by the predicate's own scope statement, and GR123's residue tripwire already fired and passed 4/4.

RIVAL 4 — ROUTE HONESTLY, ACCEPT NO SEAL. Re-parent off-epic rows to their true homes even though clause (a) reads one successor, and take exit 1. Intellectually pure, but it manufactures a NO SEAL out of a taxonomy preference when the charter's own metaphor plainly permits transit. Rejected — but it forced the ruling that transit-through-successor is legitimate, which the winner now carries explicitly.

SHARPEST ATTACK ON THE WINNER: 'You will spend the wave on 77 rows of bookkeeping judgment, while the single thing that decides SEAL vs NO SEAL — whether the guard still passes at origin/main — you have not run. If the guard fails at the tip, the triage was theater; if it passes, the triage changed nothing about the exit code.' This lands. The wave absorbs it by ordering: the guard run is cheap and goes FIRST, in survey/verify, not last, so the verdict's likely shape is known before any triage is spent. The triage is still worth doing because the exit code is not what survives the epic — the successor's readability is. And if the guard fails at the tip, the wave flips to 'diagnose, take NO SEAL', which is pre-authorized, and the triage still lands as the handoff.

SECOND ATTACK: a successor epic may ALREADY exist — gr-p5r3-successor-epic and gr-p5r5-successor-seal are both open. Filing a second one splits the residue across two addresses, and since clause (a) reads exactly one successor id, half the rows would orphan and the seal would fail for a purely clerical reason. Surveyed below as a load-bearing question.

THIRD ATTACK: re-parenting ~74 rows may be partially supported, rate-limited, or may fail silently. A partial re-parent greens nothing and corrupts the ledger. GR126 already observed a tmp-reparent-probe row appearing and vanishing mid-seal, so a concurrent session was rehearsing exactly this. Surveyed below.
Survey plan

Sixteen broad Sonnet assignments. Width is cheap now; the Digest phase distills. Every load-bearing assumption from the stress-test above appears here as ammunition for the fleets, not as a hedge on the direction.
guard-at-tip — run overflow-guard.mjs at origin/main for all three defect ids and report exit code + verbatim output. THE crux: it decides the verdict's shape.
defect-commit-provenance — does 0261ace15 actually contain the fix for EACH of GR108, GR109 and GR115, proven by diff? Or do the three need different SHAs?
successor-existence — does a successor epic already exist? Read gr-p5r3-successor-epic and gr-p5r5-successor-seal fully.
reparent-mechanics — can bp change parent_id, by what verb, does it need republish, is there a batch path, any rate limit? Find the tmp-reparent-probe evidence.
row-triage-census — classify all ~77 open rows: evidence-closeable / GUI-forward / off-epic / human-gate. By name.
offepic-rows — which live rows are plainly not Cloud GUI, and where do they truly belong?
security-shaped-rows — which open rows describe security issues, and how severe are they really?
human-gates-resolve — do all three hardcoded gates resolve via filter[_id]? Status and parent of each, especially cloud-console-billing-live-gate.
predicate-run-env — BP_TOKEN/BP_SERVER availability, Chrome availability, what a live run needs, and what the predicate does if the token is absent.
local-main-divergence — confirm all four local commits are duplicates already on origin, and that reset --hard origin/main loses nothing unique.
landed-slice-task-state — criteria state of gr-p5r7-tablet-overflow, gr-p5r7-reshoot-verify and gr-p5r8-bpconsole-dead-rule; what exactly is needed to evidence-close each.

unregistered-defect-census — which open rows self-describe as user-facing defects but are NOT in KNOWN_DEFECTS (gr-backlog-768-residue, gr-blk-modal-survives-route)? Census for DISCLOSURE, explicitly not to widen the bar.
prior-seal-papers — read the round-5 through round-8 wave Papers: what did each claim, what did each deliver, why did each fail to seal?
charter-drift — does origin's charter carry rulings beyond GR129, and is a concurrent session amending it right now?
doneset-sanity — the 63 done rows: does criteria_progress show met == total everywhere? Any obviously fake-done?
concurrent-sessions — how many worktrees are live and is another session touching cloud/ or this epic's ledger right now? GR126 risk.
DIGEST — 16 surveys folded, verify fleet in flight (round 9)
Phase: VERIFYING. What follows is the survey digest and the verify plan. The verifiers are flying against these questions now; Decide appends the wave plan after they land.
The synthesis: the verdict's shape is now largely known, and it is not the CSS

The sharpest attack on the direction — "you will spend the wave on 77 rows of bookkeeping while the thing that decides SEAL vs NO SEAL, whether the guard passes at the tip, you have not run" — was absorbed by ordering, and the answer is in: THE GUARD PASSES. overflow-guard.mjs at origin/main tip 5c058632b exits 0 for GR108, GR109, GR115 individually and for all three together, with the served-bytes==disk-bytes anti-squat assertion firing every run. The browser-geometry half of clause (b) is not the blocker. Whatever this wave's verdict is, it will not be because the CSS regressed.

The one permitted edit is factually sound. 0261ace15 is an ancestor of origin/main and was proven BY DIFF, per defect, not by commit message: GR108 = `.topbar-right > * { min-width: 0; }` at app.css:787 (breakpoint-free, because the children floor at min-width:auto and overflow at ~782px, ABOVE the 768 breakpoint); GR109 = the `.attention-row` tablet-stack block relocated to sit AFTER its base rule (source order, not specificity); GR115 = the entire `.bp-console-*` block relocated BEFORE the shared media block. Three separate non-overlapping hunks, each with in-place comments naming its GR. Registering one SHA against all three is correct, and satisfies GR129.

So both halves of clause (b) are within reach the moment gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits runs. What remains unproven is clause (a) — and nobody surveyed its IMPLEMENTATION. That is now the wave's largest unknown and the first thing the verify fleet closes.
Where the surveys correct the direction

SECOND ATTACK REFUTED AS FACT, LIVE AS RISK. No successor epic exists. Both gr-p5r3-successor-epic (0/7) and gr-p5r5-successor-seal (0/11) are open with every evidence field empty; a 2000-row ledger scan and a 1921-doc search index found zero successor-shaped top-level task. The duplicate-successor danger is therefore not a present defect but a dispatch hazard: gr-p5r5-successor-seal must be gated on a fresh open/claimed check immediately before launch, and the created successor's doc_id recorded in the charter the instant it exists.

THIRD ATTACK CONFIRMED AND QUANTIFIED. `bp task move` -> POST /v1/tasks/:doc_id/move is a real first-class endpoint with CAS + advisory lock, no republish, idempotent on same-parent. But batch:false — 74 rows is 74 POSTs, and the write bucket is 60/minute PER TOKEN, keyed to "global" for this route (no :dataset path param), SHARED with every other write the same token issues. An unthrottled loop 429s around call #61. There is no cross-row transaction: a runner that dies at row 40 leaves a mixed ledger detectable only by re-querying. And moving an in_progress row bumps its claim epoch, fencing its holder.
FOURTH ATTACK CLOSED CLEAN. 0261ace15 verified by diff per defect (above). No commit-message green here.

A FIFTH RISK THE DIRECTION DID NOT ANTICIPATE — CONCURRENCY IS NOT IDLE. Four background `gh pr merge` polling loops spawned earlier in THIS session are still alive (41min-1h28min elapsed, armed up to ~90 more minutes), targeting `^(sotg|gr-|pds-|spd-|tg-|loop-epic)` branch prefixes. They auto-merged cloud PRs #4909 and #4910 (the latter only ~9 minutes before the survey ran). They would auto-merge this round's builder PRs the instant they go green. GR126 says a verdict is valid only at an instant; these loops are a machine that moves the instant. "The predicate runs LAST, atomically, by the same agent that finished the ledger" cannot hold while they are armed.

RULING 3 IS RIGHT BUT ITS PROSE MUST BE HONEST. Of the five plainly-off-epic rows, exactly ONE has a real destination epic: gr-blk-studio-presence-perf-flake belongs to Felix pristine (task-96a908af98698118, open, 46 children, api/ improvement-only doctrine). The other four have NO owning epic anywhere in bp — repo-git-hygiene, CI/merge-gate governance and Cloud test-infra all currently live as UNPARENTED root tasks (task-openapi-drift-chronic, parent_id:null, is the same defect class as gr-blk-vercel-checks-ungoverned). The successor charter must say "no owning epic exists for this class" rather than invent a destination. And gr-blk-primary-checkout-reconcile's own body names FOUR other epics (AXI, PDS, TLV, SPD) as owners of its unpushed commits — that breakdown must survive the re-parent or a reader loses it.

THE SECURITY BAND NEEDS A GRADIENT, NOT A LABEL. Naming all five rows "security-shaped" flat would overstate the residue. Measured: 2 live-and-real (gr-bl-peer-ip-container — trust_forwarded_ip only honours loopback, so the container bridge 172.18.0.1 makes the session IP panel uniformly blind AND collapses the device-auth rate bucket to one global bucket; gr-blk-sse-token-in-query — router.ex:9707 accepts the full session bearer via query string, a credential-in-logs exposure). 1 REAL BUT NARROWER THAN WRITTEN (gr-blk-oauth-head-mint: oauth.ex:184-199 consumes the state nonce atomically on first verify, so a genuine REPLAY fails — the exposure is a first-use RACE between Plug.Head and the user's own GET, i.e. link-unfurlers and prefetchers, not attacker-controlled takeover; the charter should say "race on first use", not "replay"). 1 EXPLICITLY RULED CLEAN (gr-backlog-tfa-confirm-throttle — the session already holds the plaintext secret and can delete 2FA outright; strictly weaker than what it already grants). 1 PROSPECTIVE AND OUT-OF-BOUNDARY (gr-backlog-console-redaction-allowlist — Go, internal/provisioner, today's allowlist DOES cover every live secret; the gap is a future env var).
The finding that most threatens a readable ending

gr-p5r6-seal-finishers is lifecycle_status DONE. Its criteria 0-3 are met:true, evidencing fixes for the four user-facing defects the seal law forbids sealing over — gr-blk-modal-survives-route, gr-blk-index-icon-link, gr-blk-archives-doc-link, gr-blk-invite-ico-danger-variant — on commit f992663b4. Its criterion 7 (PR merged; lead closes the four children) is met:false. And `git merge-base --is-ancestor` proves NEITHER f992663b4 NOR its parent 6ed100cad is on origin/main. The fix never landed. The four child rows are correctly still open. But a done-marked parent row carries evidence for work that does not exist on main — the epic's signature sin wearing a ledger row instead of a commit message. This is not grounds to widen KNOWN_DEFECTS (that is rival 3, rejected as the seventh instrument). It IS grounds for the disclosure census the winner absorbs: the successor inherits four named, still-live, user-facing defects with a branch that was already written and never landed. That is a gift to the successor, not a stain — provided it is SAID.

Beyond those four, at least four more open rows self-describe user-facing defects outside the three registered ids: gr-backlog-768-residue (two symptoms; symptom (b), stacked attention rows centring their pill, may sit in GR109's SCENARIO blind spot — the committed guard measures only scenario overview-past-due, while the residue was found under panel-overview/fleet-usage), gr-backlog-setmatrix-scroll-affordance (self-downgraded: the column is REACHABLE, so an affordance gap not a clip), gr-blk-ok-danger-hue-separation (token-level root cause under GR90), gr-bl-actor-chip-cache-stale (borderline: correctness/staleness, not layout). And gr-backlog-favicon may be entirely stale — its sibling gr-blk-index-icon-link asserts favicon.ico now exists at 15,086 bytes via #4481.
The ledger, measured
140 children {open:77, done:63} at 14:09Z. Round 8 ran at 139. GR126 holds: a verdict is valid only at an instant.

Row disposition census: 11 rows evidence-closeable NOW with citable landed evidence (incl. gr-p5r8-bpconsole-dead-rule, which self-discloses "FOLDED INTO gr-p5r7-tablet-overflow" and whose 4 criteria are each independently satisfied by gr-p5r7-tablet-overflow criteria 4 and 6). 2 permanent human gates inside the roster (gr-ops-platform-admin-emails, gr-backlog-qr-live-scan-proof); the third, cloud-console-billing-live-gate, is parented under cloud-console-goal and confirmed ABSENT from this epic's 140 — it must be carried by hardcoded doc_id. 5 off-epic. 59 genuine forward.

Done-set structural read: 43/63 done rows have met==total. 20 do not. 15 fail on exactly one criterion — the epic's own "PR merged to main (the LEAD closes this, not the builder)" convention, always with evidence:"". 3 close at 0/N on a "SUPERSEDED by GR-x" close_reason. 2 have no acceptance_criteria at all but do carry a close_reason citing a landed PR. 3 fully-met rows carry no close_reason, only per-criterion evidence. Nothing is a bare unevidenced close — but read literally off criteria_progress, ~32% of this epic's "done" does not mean "all criteria satisfied".
The residue-21 tripwire already FIRED and PASSED 4/4 (GR123). Name-and-forward holds; do not re-run it.
The first act, re-measured (and it got worse during the survey)

Local main is 4 ahead / 20 behind origin/main — the brief said 18, one surveyor measured 19, the next measured 20. Origin moved twice during a five-minute survey window. Three of the four local-only commits are STRICT SUPERSETS on origin (0 local-only lines: the gui-remake charter, where origin is 5,395 B ahead carrying the entire round-8 debrief; bp-pds-charter, whose origin text names 7d2cf5a82 by hash and documents its rescue; bp-truth-grip-charter). seal-predicate.mjs is byte-identical, 13,689 B both sides. The FOURTH (1fbb59875, studio-space-priority wave-10 amendment) is NOT a byte superset: 294 local-only lines exist nowhere on origin. But no D-number is orphaned — origin carries a later, condensed, self-declared-corrective restatement of the identical D148-D160 range, landed as 4074d1986 (#4922) at 15:27:56 versus local's 14:02:13 draft. The reset is safe. The wave must NOT claim all four are byte-identical duplicates: three are strict supersets, one is a superseded rewrite, and 4074d1986/#4922 is the version of record.

The reset is also PREREQUISITE, not hygiene: overflow-guard.mjs does not exist in the unreset local working tree, so running seal-predicate.mjs there reports all three KNOWN_DEFECTS as "guard is NOT COMMITTED" — a FALSE NO SEAL manufactured by stale local state.
COVERAGE MAP — what was checked and FOUND

BP_TOKEN is unset in this shell and it does NOT matter: /v1/data/query/:dataset/:type is documented [public] (docs/api-v1.md:55) and returned 200 with real data under `Bearer undefined`, under a garbage token, and with no header at all.

COVERAGE MAP — what was checked and NOT FOUND (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

CORNERS NO SURVEYOR REACHED

CLAUSE (A)'S IMPLEMENTATION. The single largest gap. Not one surveyor read what seal-predicate.mjs actually REQUIRES of a row to satisfy clause (a): which field carries "a named forwarding address", what counts as "an evidence-closure", whether a human-gate LABEL is a distinct third disposition, and whether parent==successor alone suffices. The entire triage plan is built on an unread contract. This is verify assignment 1.

THE PREDICATE HAS NEVER BEEN RUN BY THIS WAVE. Every claim about its behaviour is inherited from round 8's debrief or read off source. Its exact current failure text, its crash-vs-verdict boundary, and whether it consumes the guard's PASS correctly through its own invocation path (different CWD, port, Chrome discovery) are all unproven here.

bp task move was never EXERCISED. The surveyor held the read-only line deliberately and traced source instead — correct discipline, but it means no live round-trip, no observed 429, and no confirmation that the destination-visibility query actually shows a moved row.

The 11 evidence-closeable rows were classified from the charter's own GR narrative. Three of them (gr-backlog-fleetstrip-dead-code, gr-backlog-cap-payload-drift, task-050074a198b116c4) are cited by DESCRIPTION, not by literal SHA. Closing them on prose would be the commit-message sin one layer up.
No surveyor ran the guard against the scenarios where gr-backlog-768-residue was found (panel-overview, fleet-usage) — only overview-past-due, which is all the frozen guard measures.
No full worktree sweep for dirty in-progress edits (1,139 registered worktrees; the scan timed out at two minutes). Only the two tied to this epic's merged branch were checked, both clean.
js/, api/ outside cloud/, and the Go surfaces were untouched by every surveyor — correct, the surface fence forbids them, but it means this wave has no read on whether anything there moved.
VERIFY PLAN — 8 assignments, in flight now

This is the LAST look before the plan is cut. Every assignment either closes a Decide-critical unknown or proves a load-bearing survey claim by RUNNING something. Nothing here browses, and nothing here builds a seventh instrument — every assignment reads or runs an artifact that already exists.

v1 clause-a-contract (opus, worktree, RUNS the predicate against synthetic rosters): read seal-predicate.mjs clause (a) line by line and PROVE by execution what a row must carry to satisfy it. Does parent==successor alone pass? Is a human-gate label a distinct disposition, and what exact field/value does it read? Does an evidence-closed row need lifecycle done, or criteria met, or both? Feed it hand-built roster fixtures that pass and that fail, and report the exact boundary. The whole triage plan rests on this contract.

v2 predicate-live-run (opus, worktree, RUNS seal-predicate.mjs at origin/main): capture verbatim stdout + exit code TODAY, unedited, so the wave knows the failure text it must move. Confirm the crash-vs-verdict boundary: that the two unwrapped fetchRoster calls really do throw without a VERDICT banner, and that a run WITHOUT the "=== SEAL PREDICATE ===" banner is distinguishable from a substantive NO SEAL by more than the exit code. Also confirm the predicate consumes the guard's exit-0 PASS through its OWN invocation path.

v3 reparent-live-proof (sonnet, RUNS bp task move on a throwaway row): create a scratch task, move it, confirm via GET /v1/data/query/production/task?filter[parent_id]=..., move it back, delete it. Then measure the real throttle: issue ~15 rapid moves against the scratch row and report whether 429 arrives, at what count, and what retry-after says. Produce the exact throttled script shape a 74-row run must use.

NOT FOUND, decisive: no successor epic existed anywhere - a 2000-row ledger scan, the 1921-doc search index, the 140-child roster and the charter all came back negative, and both gr-p5r3-successor-epic and gr-p5r5-successor-seal sat open at 0/7 and 0/11 with every evidence field empty.

NOT FOUND: no forwarding_address, close_reason, acceptance_criteria, evidence, label, tags or priority field is read anywhere in seal-predicate.mjs. 'label' and 'evidence' occur only inside prose output strings at lines 11, 214 and 231.
NOT FOUND: no committed script anywhere in the repo defines the gh-pr-merge loop pattern (grep across *.js/*.md/*.sh) - it is always agent-improvised, so there is no single kill switch.
NOT FOUND: the charter never recorded the merge SHA its own landing produced (grep -c '7a5aff656' returned 0). That omission is the root cause of the branch-SHA citation error.

NOT FOUND: no owning epic exists in bp for repo-git hygiene, CI/merge-gate governance or Cloud test-infrastructure. task-openapi-drift-chronic sits unparented at root in the same class. That absence IS the finding.

NOT FOUND: 'absent BP_TOKEN' is not a failure mode - the roster route serves unauthenticated and the two runs are byte-identical apart from the timestamp. The repair budget was reserved for something that cannot happen.

PARTIAL, named as unchecked: the rest of the done-set was NOT swept for the branch-SHA error class. The roster payload is summary-shaped (4 hex-like strings across all 140 rows, none of them commits), so a real audit needs 140 per-row calls. Filed as gr-bl-doneset-merge-sha-reaudit rather than claimed clean.
PARTIAL: the 86-scenario GR109 census ran light-theme only; the four attention-row scenarios were measured in both themes and were identical, but for the other 82 dark is inferred, not measured.
Decisions
GR130 - cite MERGE SHAs, never branch SHAs. Why: origin/main is a linear squash chain, so a branch head can never be an ancestor, and that one error declared four landed fixes unlanded.

GR131/GR132 - clause (a) reads three fields and the forwarded branch is dead code live. Why: the re-parents cannot produce an impossible green, so the risk is narrative, not mechanical - and the banner will read '0 forwarded by name' after a perfect triage, so the charter must carry the roster delta and census alongside the stdout.
GR133 - absence of a VERDICT line is a crash, never a verdict. Why: crash and NO SEAL both exit 1, so recording the exit code alone could fabricate an ending.
GR134/GR135 - settle and confirm the three gates before running, and run from the repo root. Why: both produce a false NO SEAL with a full banner that the crash test cannot catch.

GR136 - Decide filed the successor itself, cloud-console-hardening-epic. Why: the predicate never validates the successor id, so a typo yields a silent 74 orphans; filing it here kills both the typo and the duplication hazard, and a chartered successor is judgment work, not builder work.
GR137 - the four seal-finisher defects are evidence-CLOSED, not forwarded. Why: forwarding them would tell the next reader the epic left four user-facing defects unfixed when it fixed all four.
GR138 - cloud-console-billing-live-gate stays under cloud-console-goal. Why: bucket (c) is parent-independent, so moving it would strip the billing epic of its own gate for zero mechanical gain.

GR139 - do NOT reset local main. Why: at Decide the primary checkout was dirty with a concurrent session's 249 uncommitted lines, and a detached worktree at origin/main serves the reset's purpose without destroying them.
GR140 - the disclosure census is named and forwarded, never widened. Why: re-deriving the bar after seeing the roster is exactly what the freeze forbids, and it is how an epic never closes.

Decide performed the successor filing and the disposition DECISIONS itself, and handed only the throttled execution to a builder. Why: two agents writing the same rows would collide on a shared 60/min bucket with no partial-failure detection.
The wave — three slices, two rounds

Round 1 dispatches two dependency-free slices with disjoint file sets. Round 2 is the terminal act, and it does NOT dispatch beside them: the predicate reads origin/main, so clause (b) stays structurally unsatisfiable until the defect commits are merged, and re-parenting before the disposition pass would sweep work that actually shipped into the successor.

ROUND 1 - gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits (opus). Surface: the frozen predicate. Files: cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.mjs. The ONE permitted edit, commit:null -> 0261ace15 on all three KNOWN_DEFECTS rows. Gate: node --check cloud/priv/static/app.js && node cloud/priv/static/__app.test.mjs, plus git merge-base --is-ancestor 0261ace15 origin/main and a repo-root predicate run showing three clause-(b) checkmarks.

ROUND 1 - gr-p5r9-disposition-pass (opus). Surface: the bp ledger only, zero files, no branch, no PR by design. Executes an 18-row disposition table: 11 closes on diff-verified merge SHAs, 3 merge-gated criteria the lead closes (round 8's inherited steps 1 and 2), 4 honest ruling-closes that must say they are ruling-closes. Two SHAs are forbidden as evidence - fcafc0d82 and 3d80a58bf - because neither resolves on origin/main. Gate: a bracket-encoded filter[parent_id] re-derivation showing the live count before and after.

ROUND 2 - gr-p5r5-successor-seal (opus), after: [gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits, gr-p5r9-disposition-pass]. Surface: the ledger plus the charter. Re-parents survivors into cloud-console-hardening-epic and runs the predicate LAST, once, atomically, from the repo root, with --successor, after sweeping the merge loops and confirming all three gates resolve. Gate: the predicate's own verbatim stdout, stderr and exit code.

Round 1 is deliberately thin, and that is the point. Every act in this wave is disclosure, bookkeeping, or verification of an artifact that already exists. Rounds 3-7 each discovered its evidence was thinner than its claim and spawned a new instrument; the seal receded by exactly one instrument per round. A seventh widening is not rigor.
Backlog filed now, not deferred silently
gr-bl-doneset-merge-sha-reaudit (p1, under the successor) - the rest of the done-set is UNCHECKED for the branch-SHA error class; a real audit needs 140 per-row calls that were not spent.

gr-bl-overflow-guard-route-blind (p2, under the successor) - the guard never applies a scenario deepLink, so every instance-detail panel is unreachable by it, and GR109 samples 1 of the 4 scenarios that render .attention-row. The gap was measured and found EMPTY, which is why it is named rather than widened.

gr-bl-close-convention-unmet-criteria (p3, under the successor) - 20 of 63 done rows do not read as 'all criteria satisfied': 15 park an unstamped merge criterion, 3 close at 0/N on superseded reasons, 2 carry no criteria at all. Nothing is fabricated; the ledger just does not read literally.

task-bp-create-drops-long-description (p2, top-level) - bp doc create silently discards a long multi-line --set description and the failure only surfaces later as an unrelated publish-wall rejection. Hit twice during this Decide.

task-label-spine-details-null (p3, top-level) - the label_spine 422's own hint promises a per-field details payload and returns null, so the author cannot tell which of six rules broke. Diagnosis took five round trips and was solved only by reading the Elixir source.
DEBRIEF - round 1 built and reviewed, grade A

Phase: COMPLETE for round 1. Two slices dispatched, two green, both reviewed adversarially and re-gated on their final state. Round 2 (gr-p5r5-successor-seal) is deferred by the sequenced-rounds law, not stalled. The seal itself has NOT landed and this debrief does not pretend it did: the live predicate at review time still returns VERDICT: NO SEAL. What changed is WHICH clause blocks it. Clause (b) is now fully green; clause (a) is the sole remaining blocker, exactly as Decide predicted.
What shipped

gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits -> loop-epic/register-the-diff-proven-defect-commit-t-0 (unchanged by review; no -r commits were needed). VERDICT: correct and exactly scoped. The diff is 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-) - commit:null -> '0261ace15' on all three KNOWN_DEFECTS rows, each with an in-place comment naming its landed hunk. The freeze held in every direction the reviewer checked: no clause body, no threshold, no SWEEP envelope field, no guard delegation, and the SEAL banner deliberately untouched despite round 9 proving it under-reports the triage (GR132 - that disclosure is charter business, not an edit to the instrument). Each named hunk was verified present on origin/main: .topbar-right > * { min-width: 0 } at app.css:787; the .attention-row tablet-stack block at app.css:2704-2713, carrying its own source-order rationale; the .bp-console-* bases at app.css:2420-2477. Merge-SHA discipline held under control - 0261ace15 IS-ancestor exit 0, the same fix's branch head e4bb4bfae NOT-ancestor exit 1.

Reviewer re-ran the full gate on the final tree: node --check OK; 640/640 app tests pass, 0 fail; ANCESTOR_OK; and a live repo-root predicate run at 2026-07-20T15:22:40.525Z printing CLAUSE (b) with three checkmarks and zero NO-COMMIT lines. The browser guard actually launched three times - no --guard-cmd stub, which was the obvious way to fake this and the builder did not take it. Roster at that run: 142 children {in_progress:2, open:60, done:80}, live 62, orphans 60, all three bucket-(c) gates resolving.

gr-p5r9-disposition-pass -> no branch and no PR, by design (pure ledger; git status --porcelain empty). VERDICT: strong, and honest about its own failures. 16 rows closed done, each confirmed by re-reading lifecycle_status from the server rather than trusting an HTTP 200. Live count 77 -> 61; the post-pass read of 62 is 61 plus one residue task the pass itself filed, not a failed close. Ancestry was re-verified at execution time against origin/main @ 0044903a4 for all seven cited merge SHAs, with three controls proving the check can fail (e4bb4bfae, fcafc0d82, 3d80a58bf all exit 1). The reviewer grepped the entire 142-row roster for the two forbidden SHAs: every occurrence sits inside its own explicit refusal sentence, never as evidence. The four GROUP 3 rows open with a literal 'THIS IS A RULING-CLOSE, NOT A COMMIT-CLOSE' and leave their criteria unflipped, so a ruling is never dressed as per-criterion proof. Invariants held on server read-back: gr-p5r4-spa-b still open 0/7, gr-backlog-css-brace-detector still open 1/4, the brace tripwire intact, seal-predicate.mjs and overflow-guard.mjs byte-identical to origin/main.
Two honest declines, both verified and both correct

gr-p5r7-reshoot-verify criterion 8 already reads met with STRONGER evidence than the brief prescribed - 'PR #4910 MERGED 2026-07-20T14:01:13Z', a real merged PR, not 'no PR by design'. Writing the brief's text would have replaced a true fact with a false one and downgraded genuine merge evidence. gr-p5r6-seal-finishers criterion 7 is structurally unstampable: the row is lifecycle=done, so claim returns not_ready and stamp returns not_in_progress:done. Recorded as a MISS with the server's verbatim errors, never forced, and filed as published residue gr-p5r9-seal-finishers-crit7-unstampable. A brief whose premise has gone stale is refused, not obeyed - that is the behaviour this epic spent six rounds learning, and seeing it appear unprompted in a builder is the healthiest signal in the wave.

One declared deviation, and the reviewer agrees with it: gr-p5r7-tablet-overflow was a stamp-only GROUP 2 row, but stamping required claiming it, which moved it open -> in_progress under a foreign claim. Leaving a fully-met (11/11) landed row stranded under a foreign claim would have FORWARDED it - the exact sin this slice exists to prevent - so the builder closed it and declared the reasoning in the close_reason. Trivially reopenable, every criterion carries its own proof.
The wave's own instrument bit it once, and it said so

The disposition driver's rate-limit detector matched the response TEXT for '429' and 'rate_limited' instead of the HTTP status or the structured error object. Both strings occur in legitimate payloads - a rev digest containing '429', and a sibling task's brief that literally discusses rate_limited and retry_after. Every throttle line in its log is a FALSE POSITIVE over document content; ZERO confirmed HTTP 429s were hit, and 12 spurious claim epochs were burned on one row before it noticed. No outcome changed - every affected row was completed and read back - but it is the measure-the-thing-not-a-proxy failure committed by the instrument built to avoid it. It was disclosed in full, in the ledger, unprompted.
Ledger audit - outcome and reviewer fixes

Both slice tasks were claimed before work, stamped per-criterion as the work happened (not batched), and left lifecycle=in_progress with their merge-gated criteria UNMET for the lead - gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits 4/5 (criterion 4 = PR merged), gr-p5r9-disposition-pass 6/8 (criterion 7 = no PR by design; criterion 2 = the GROUP 2 miss). The rows touched during the disposition window (15:11-15:21) are exactly the 16 closes plus the one residue task plus its own row; nothing outside the wave was moved. The successor cloud-console-hardening-epic reads back published, top-level, with ZERO children - the re-parenting is round 2's entire substance.

FIX 1 - gr-backlog-768-residue criteria 0 and 2 still rested on the non-ancestor branch SHA 3d80a58bf as their stored proof. That is the exact sin the disposition exists to kill, surviving one layer down in inherited evidence text while only the close_reason corrected it. Both criteria now carry a dated reviewer correction naming the on-main content anchor (app.css:4393-4413, re-verified: .dom-rung{max-width:100%;min-width:0} and .dom-rung-code{white-space:normal;overflow-wrap:anywhere}) and the re-run gate numbers.

FIX 2 - gr-p5r9-disposition-pass criterion 2's honest MISS lived only in the builder's report, not the ledger; its evidence field was empty. The full three-part rationale (1 actioned, 2 declined on a stale premise, each verified by the reviewer against the server) is now stored on the criterion itself, still unmet.
Grade: A

What earns it: the wish was to run the seal predicate and abide by it without building a seventh instrument, and that is precisely what happened. Round 1 created nothing. It edited three lines of an existing frozen file and moved 16 ledger rows. Clause (b) went from structurally unsatisfiable to live-green with a real browser guard executing three times, and the verdict is still reported as NO SEAL rather than negotiated. Both builders distrusted their own green - one ran the gate twice and explicitly refused the stubbed-guard shortcut; the other re-verified seven merge SHAs at execution time WITH three failing controls, refused two stale brief instructions rather than obeying them into a falsehood, and disclosed a self-inflicted false-positive bug that changed no outcome and that nobody would ever have found.

What falls short of A+: the disposition driver's 429 detector was a proxy-not-thing measurement in the instrument built to end proxy measurements - caught and disclosed, but it should not have shipped. Two criteria on gr-backlog-768-residue were left resting on a forbidden branch SHA, one layer below where the close_reason corrected it, which the reviewer had to fix - the discipline was applied to close_reasons but not swept through inherited criterion evidence. And the seal SHIPS UNSEALED for the seventh time: this wave earned its grade on process, not on an ending. The instructed short SHA '0261ace15' is unambiguous today and left as Decide specified, but a colliding prefix would fail it closed - noted, not changed, because unnecessary deviation from a frozen-file instruction is the worse sin.
What the next wave takes
(1) Merge loop-epic/register-the-diff-proven-defect-commit-t-0. The LEAD closes gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits criterion 4 (PR merged) - the builder correctly did not.
(2) The LEAD closes gr-p5r9-disposition-pass criterion 7 as 'no PR by design', NOT abandoned, and leaves criterion 2 unmet with its now-recorded MISS.

(3) THEN and only then dispatch gr-p5r5-successor-seal. It cannot run before (1) MERGES: the predicate reads d.commit from the file at origin/main, so a pre-merge run either reads null (a false NO SEAL on clause b) or silently certifies off an unmerged branch.

(4) Round 2's own traps, unchanged: re-parent the ~60 survivors into cloud-console-hardening-epic and re-parent ITSELF LAST (it is a direct child of the epic and will be in_progress at run time, so clause (a) counts it as an orphan); sweep merge daemons three times; confirm all three bucket-(c) gates with standalone bracket-encoded filter[_id] queries (fetchById swallows every error, so one 429 forces NO SEAL with clause (a) perfectly clean); run the predicate ONCE, from the repo root, with --successor.

(5) Read the result honestly: a crash and a NO SEAL both exit 1, and absence of a VERDICT: line is a CRASH, never a verdict (GR133). Expect the banner to read '0 forwarded by name' after a perfect triage - that is STRUCTURAL (GR132), so record the roster delta and the per-row census alongside the verbatim stdout.

Cloud GUI Remake — Wave 5 round 9: RUN THE PREDICATE, TAKE THE VERDICT

Living wave Paper for the Cloud GUI Remake epic (bp task task-47bc4168392dec17), round 9 of phase 5. Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md (the epic's law — NOT the rotating bp-cloud-epic-charter.md slot). Predecessor Paper: cloud-gui-remake-wave-2026-07-20-seal-r4.

STATUS: SURVEYING. This Paper is appended by every later phase — Digest adds the survey digest and verify plan, Decide adds the decisions and wave plan, Review closes it as the debrief.

The wish

"RUN THE SEAL PREDICATE AND ABIDE BY IT. The Cloud GUI Remake epic has now attempted to seal SIX times. Round 8 built the thing that ends that: an executable seal predicate, frozen and committed BEFORE any builder flew. This cycle executes it and takes the verdict — SEAL or NO SEAL — without negotiation and without building a seventh instrument."

Hard model constraint: every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet. Decide MUST set builder_model 'opus' for EVERY slice, never 'fable'.

Ground truth, verified at Strategize

The inherited dispatch order (from round 8's debrief, origin charter tail)

Direction: THE SEAL IS A DISCLOSURE, NOT A RENAME

Execute the inherited dispatch order exactly, build NO new instrument, and take the exit code as the verdict. That is the wish, and it is non-negotiable. But the exit code is not the deliverable. The predicate can only measure a mechanical property — 'does this row's parent equal the successor id'. A successor epic with no charter, no triage and no priorities passes clause (a) identically to a great one. What survives this epic is not the exit code; it is whether the next person can READ the ending.

So the wave's product is a seal that means what a reader thinks it means:

FIRST ACT, BEFORE ANY BUILDER FLIES: reset local main to origin/main. Four duplicate charter commits sit on local main while origin's charter runs 5,395 bytes ahead. This is the known epic-cycle-commits-charter-to-local-main trap, and it poisons every worktree based on it.

Direction debate

RIVAL 1 — MECHANICAL EXECUTION. Do the four dispatch steps, bulk re-parent the survivors, run, report. The most literal reading of the wish and the cheapest. It wins on 'no seventh instrument' purity. It loses because it produces a seal that is a rename: 74 rows land in an unchartered bucket, several of them mislabeled as Cloud GUI work when they are repo hygiene or Studio, and a reader six months out finds a successor with no story. The predicate cannot detect any of that — which is precisely why the wave, not the instrument, has to supply it.

RIVAL 2 — DISCLOSURE SEAL (WINNER). The same four steps, but every row gets an individual disposition and the successor is chartered and triaged. Costs one slice of judgment work. It wins because the exit code is guaranteed-ish either way — what actually varies between a good and a bad version of this wave is whether the ending is readable.

RIVAL 3 — AUDIT FIRST. Before sealing, spot-audit the 63 done rows for false-done and widen KNOWN_DEFECTS to cover every ledger row that self-describes as user-facing. REJECTED: this is the seventh instrument in disguise. It re-derives the bar after seeing the roster, which is the exact thing the freeze exists to forbid. Its legitimate concern — that clause (b) certifies the word KNOWN over only three hand-registered defects — is already disclosed by the predicate's own scope statement, and GR123's residue tripwire already fired and passed 4/4.

RIVAL 4 — ROUTE HONESTLY, ACCEPT NO SEAL. Re-parent off-epic rows to their true homes even though clause (a) reads one successor, and take exit 1. Intellectually pure, but it manufactures a NO SEAL out of a taxonomy preference when the charter's own metaphor plainly permits transit. Rejected — but it forced the ruling that transit-through-successor is legitimate, which the winner now carries explicitly.

SHARPEST ATTACK ON THE WINNER: 'You will spend the wave on 77 rows of bookkeeping judgment, while the single thing that decides SEAL vs NO SEAL — whether the guard still passes at origin/main — you have not run. If the guard fails at the tip, the triage was theater; if it passes, the triage changed nothing about the exit code.' This lands. The wave absorbs it by ordering: the guard run is cheap and goes FIRST, in survey/verify, not last, so the verdict's likely shape is known before any triage is spent. The triage is still worth doing because the exit code is not what survives the epic — the successor's readability is. And if the guard fails at the tip, the wave flips to 'diagnose, take NO SEAL', which is pre-authorized, and the triage still lands as the handoff.

SECOND ATTACK: a successor epic may ALREADY exist — gr-p5r3-successor-epic and gr-p5r5-successor-seal are both open. Filing a second one splits the residue across two addresses, and since clause (a) reads exactly one successor id, half the rows would orphan and the seal would fail for a purely clerical reason. Surveyed below as a load-bearing question.

THIRD ATTACK: re-parenting ~74 rows may be partially supported, rate-limited, or may fail silently. A partial re-parent greens nothing and corrupts the ledger. GR126 already observed a tmp-reparent-probe row appearing and vanishing mid-seal, so a concurrent session was rehearsing exactly this. Surveyed below.

Survey plan

Sixteen broad Sonnet assignments. Width is cheap now; the Digest phase distills. Every load-bearing assumption from the stress-test above appears here as ammunition for the fleets, not as a hedge on the direction.

DIGEST — 16 surveys folded, verify fleet in flight (round 9)

Phase: VERIFYING. What follows is the survey digest and the verify plan. The verifiers are flying against these questions now; Decide appends the wave plan after they land.

The synthesis: the verdict's shape is now largely known, and it is not the CSS

The sharpest attack on the direction — "you will spend the wave on 77 rows of bookkeeping while the thing that decides SEAL vs NO SEAL, whether the guard passes at the tip, you have not run" — was absorbed by ordering, and the answer is in: THE GUARD PASSES. overflow-guard.mjs at origin/main tip 5c058632b exits 0 for GR108, GR109, GR115 individually and for all three together, with the served-bytes==disk-bytes anti-squat assertion firing every run. The browser-geometry half of clause (b) is not the blocker. Whatever this wave's verdict is, it will not be because the CSS regressed.

The one permitted edit is factually sound. 0261ace15 is an ancestor of origin/main and was proven BY DIFF, per defect, not by commit message: GR108 = `.topbar-right > * { min-width: 0; }` at app.css:787 (breakpoint-free, because the children floor at min-width:auto and overflow at ~782px, ABOVE the 768 breakpoint); GR109 = the `.attention-row` tablet-stack block relocated to sit AFTER its base rule (source order, not specificity); GR115 = the entire `.bp-console-*` block relocated BEFORE the shared media block. Three separate non-overlapping hunks, each with in-place comments naming its GR. Registering one SHA against all three is correct, and satisfies GR129.

So both halves of clause (b) are within reach the moment gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits runs. What remains unproven is clause (a) — and nobody surveyed its IMPLEMENTATION. That is now the wave's largest unknown and the first thing the verify fleet closes.

Where the surveys correct the direction

The finding that most threatens a readable ending

gr-p5r6-seal-finishers is lifecycle_status DONE. Its criteria 0-3 are met:true, evidencing fixes for the four user-facing defects the seal law forbids sealing over — gr-blk-modal-survives-route, gr-blk-index-icon-link, gr-blk-archives-doc-link, gr-blk-invite-ico-danger-variant — on commit f992663b4. Its criterion 7 (PR merged; lead closes the four children) is met:false. And `git merge-base --is-ancestor` proves NEITHER f992663b4 NOR its parent 6ed100cad is on origin/main. The fix never landed. The four child rows are correctly still open. But a done-marked parent row carries evidence for work that does not exist on main — the epic's signature sin wearing a ledger row instead of a commit message. This is not grounds to widen KNOWN_DEFECTS (that is rival 3, rejected as the seventh instrument). It IS grounds for the disclosure census the winner absorbs: the successor inherits four named, still-live, user-facing defects with a branch that was already written and never landed. That is a gift to the successor, not a stain — provided it is SAID.

Beyond those four, at least four more open rows self-describe user-facing defects outside the three registered ids: gr-backlog-768-residue (two symptoms; symptom (b), stacked attention rows centring their pill, may sit in GR109's SCENARIO blind spot — the committed guard measures only scenario overview-past-due, while the residue was found under panel-overview/fleet-usage), gr-backlog-setmatrix-scroll-affordance (self-downgraded: the column is REACHABLE, so an affordance gap not a clip), gr-blk-ok-danger-hue-separation (token-level root cause under GR90), gr-bl-actor-chip-cache-stale (borderline: correctness/staleness, not layout). And gr-backlog-favicon may be entirely stale — its sibling gr-blk-index-icon-link asserts favicon.ico now exists at 15,086 bytes via #4481.

The ledger, measured

The first act, re-measured (and it got worse during the survey)

Local main is 4 ahead / 20 behind origin/main — the brief said 18, one surveyor measured 19, the next measured 20. Origin moved twice during a five-minute survey window. Three of the four local-only commits are STRICT SUPERSETS on origin (0 local-only lines: the gui-remake charter, where origin is 5,395 B ahead carrying the entire round-8 debrief; bp-pds-charter, whose origin text names 7d2cf5a82 by hash and documents its rescue; bp-truth-grip-charter). seal-predicate.mjs is byte-identical, 13,689 B both sides. The FOURTH (1fbb59875, studio-space-priority wave-10 amendment) is NOT a byte superset: 294 local-only lines exist nowhere on origin. But no D-number is orphaned — origin carries a later, condensed, self-declared-corrective restatement of the identical D148-D160 range, landed as 4074d1986 (#4922) at 15:27:56 versus local's 14:02:13 draft. The reset is safe. The wave must NOT claim all four are byte-identical duplicates: three are strict supersets, one is a superseded rewrite, and 4074d1986/#4922 is the version of record.

The reset is also PREREQUISITE, not hygiene: overflow-guard.mjs does not exist in the unreset local working tree, so running seal-predicate.mjs there reports all three KNOWN_DEFECTS as "guard is NOT COMMITTED" — a FALSE NO SEAL manufactured by stale local state.

COVERAGE MAP — what was checked and FOUND

COVERAGE MAP — what was checked and NOT FOUND (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

CORNERS NO SURVEYOR REACHED

VERIFY PLAN — 8 assignments, in flight now

This is the LAST look before the plan is cut. Every assignment either closes a Decide-critical unknown or proves a load-bearing survey claim by RUNNING something. Nothing here browses, and nothing here builds a seventh instrument — every assignment reads or runs an artifact that already exists.

Model split rationale: opus on v1, v2, v5, v7 — the four places where being wrong is expensive (an unread contract, a misread verdict, a false-done judgment call, and a scenario blind spot that would let the wave overstate what the guard proved). Sonnet on v3, v4, v6, v8 — mechanical proofs with unambiguous pass/fail.

Pre-authorized already, and unchanged by anything the survey found: NO SEAL is terminal. One repair attempt on a MECHANICAL failure only (missing Chrome, absent network, a crash without the VERDICT banner). A substantive failure IS the verdict, and the named successor is the ending. No seventh instrument, in any disguise.

DECIDE — verification results, decisions, and the wave plan

Eight verifiers ran. They confirmed the direction's thesis and contradicted the inherited brief in nine places. Where verification contradicted the direction, the evidence wins. The corrections land in the charter as GR130-GR141 (PR #4940).

What the verifiers proved and refuted

PROVEN — the guard is healthy at the tip, so clause (b) is not the blocker. overflow-guard.mjs exits 0 and prints PASS for GR108, GR109 and GR115 individually and combined: "0/44 overflowing across 721-1440 (sweep includes 769/775/780/785 - ABOVE the breakpoint)", with the served-bytes == disk-bytes anti-squat assertion firing every run, and exit 2 on an unknown --defect id (no vacuous pass).

PROVEN — the one permitted edit is mechanically sufficient, demonstrated live. With commit:null -> '0261ace15' the live run turns clause (b) fully green (three checkmarks) and the verdict reduces to a single cause: "- 74 live row(s) carry no forwarding address". The probe edit reverted clean.                               Reviewer re-ran the full gate on the final tree: node --check OK; 640/640 app tests pass, 0 fail; ANCESTOR_OK; and a live repo-root predicate run at 2026-07-20T15:22:40.525Z printing CLAUSE (b) with three checkmarks and zero NO-COMMIT lines. The browser guard actually launched three times - no --guard-cmd stub, which was the obvious way to fake this and the builder did not take it. Roster at that run: 142 children {in_progress:2, open:60, done:80}, live 62, orphans 60, all three bucket-(c) gates resolving.

                              gr-p5r9-disposition-pass -> no branch and no PR, by design (pure ledger; git status --porcelain empty). VERDICT: strong, and honest about its own failures. 16 rows closed done, each confirmed by re-reading lifecycle_status from the server rather than trusting an HTTP 200. Live count 77 -> 61; the post-pass read of 62 is 61 plus one residue task the pass itself filed, not a failed close. Ancestry was re-verified at execution time against origin/main @ 0044903a4 for all seven cited merge SHAs, with three controls proving the check can fail (e4bb4bfae, fcafc0d82, 3d80a58bf all exit 1). The reviewer grepped the entire 142-row roster for the two forbidden SHAs: every occurrence sits inside its own explicit refusal sentence, never as evidence. The four GROUP 3 rows open with a literal 'THIS IS A RULING-CLOSE, NOT A COMMIT-CLOSE' and leave their criteria unflipped, so a ruling is never dressed as per-criterion proof. Invariants held on server read-back: gr-p5r4-spa-b still open 0/7, gr-backlog-css-brace-detector still open 1/4, the brace tripwire intact, seal-predicate.mjs and overflow-guard.mjs byte-identical to origin/main.

                              Two honest declines, both verified and both correct

                              gr-p5r7-reshoot-verify criterion 8 already reads met with STRONGER evidence than the brief prescribed - 'PR #4910 MERGED 2026-07-20T14:01:13Z', a real merged PR, not 'no PR by design'. Writing the brief's text would have replaced a true fact with a false one and downgraded genuine merge evidence. gr-p5r6-seal-finishers criterion 7 is structurally unstampable: the row is lifecycle=done, so claim returns not_ready and stamp returns not_in_progress:done. Recorded as a MISS with the server's verbatim errors, never forced, and filed as published residue gr-p5r9-seal-finishers-crit7-unstampable. A brief whose premise has gone stale is refused, not obeyed - that is the behaviour this epic spent six rounds learning, and seeing it appear unprompted in a builder is the healthiest signal in the wave.

                              One declared deviation, and the reviewer agrees with it: gr-p5r7-tablet-overflow was a stamp-only GROUP 2 row, but stamping required claiming it, which moved it open -> in_progress under a foreign claim. Leaving a fully-met (11/11) landed row stranded under a foreign claim would have FORWARDED it - the exact sin this slice exists to prevent - so the builder closed it and declared the reasoning in the close_reason. Trivially reopenable, every criterion carries its own proof.

                              The wave's own instrument bit it once, and it said so

                              The disposition driver's rate-limit detector matched the response TEXT for '429' and 'rate_limited' instead of the HTTP status or the structured error object. Both strings occur in legitimate payloads - a rev digest containing '429', and a sibling task's brief that literally discusses rate_limited and retry_after. Every throttle line in its log is a FALSE POSITIVE over document content; ZERO confirmed HTTP 429s were hit, and 12 spurious claim epochs were burned on one row before it noticed. No outcome changed - every affected row was completed and read back - but it is the measure-the-thing-not-a-proxy failure committed by the instrument built to avoid it. It was disclosed in full, in the ledger, unprompted.

                              Ledger audit - outcome and reviewer fixes

                              Both slice tasks were claimed before work, stamped per-criterion as the work happened (not batched), and left lifecycle=in_progress with their merge-gated criteria UNMET for the lead - gr-p5r8-register-defect-commits 4/5 (criterion 4 = PR merged), gr-p5r9-disposition-pass 6/8 (criterion 7 = no PR by design; criterion 2 = the GROUP 2 miss). The rows touched during the disposition window (15:11-15:21) are exactly the 16 closes plus the one residue task plus its own row; nothing outside the wave was moved. The successor cloud-console-hardening-epic reads back published, top-level, with ZERO children - the re-parenting is round 2's entire substance.

                                Grade: A

                                What earns it: the wish was to run the seal predicate and abide by it without building a seventh instrument, and that is precisely what happened. Round 1 created nothing. It edited three lines of an existing frozen file and moved 16 ledger rows. Clause (b) went from structurally unsatisfiable to live-green with a real browser guard executing three times, and the verdict is still reported as NO SEAL rather than negotiated. Both builders distrusted their own green - one ran the gate twice and explicitly refused the stubbed-guard shortcut; the other re-verified seven merge SHAs at execution time WITH three failing controls, refused two stale brief instructions rather than obeying them into a falsehood, and disclosed a self-inflicted false-positive bug that changed no outcome and that nobody would ever have found.

                                What falls short of A+: the disposition driver's 429 detector was a proxy-not-thing measurement in the instrument built to end proxy measurements - caught and disclosed, but it should not have shipped. Two criteria on gr-backlog-768-residue were left resting on a forbidden branch SHA, one layer below where the close_reason corrected it, which the reviewer had to fix - the discipline was applied to close_reasons but not swept through inherited criterion evidence. And the seal SHIPS UNSEALED for the seventh time: this wave earned its grade on process, not on an ending.
